key_insight: LLMs can partially infer viewpoint rotation from language alone, and interpretability analyses show that both LLMs and VLMs encode rotation-related signals via distinct internal mechanisms—visual grounding alters representations but is not strictly required for basic rotation reasoning.
problem_solved: Determines whether linguistic intelligence by itself suffices for spatial reasoning about viewpoint rotation and uncovers how LLMs and VLMs internally perform rotation-related tasks when visual inputs are absent.
method: Construct controlled text-only viewpoint-rotation tasks and prompts that describe scenes and rotation operations.
Benchmark and compare LLM and VLM behavior on these tasks using zero-shot/finetuned prompting, ablations, and behavioral probes.
Perform interpretability analyses (attention/activation inspection, probing classifiers, and causal interventions such as neuron/attention ablation) to localize rotation representations.
impact: Clarifies the capabilities and limits of text-only spatial reasoning, guiding model selection, prompt engineering, and interpretability strategies for applications (robotics, AR, multimodal systems) where visual inputs may be limited or absent.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: dataset → models (LLM vs VLM) → behavioral tests → interpretability tools (probes, ablations).
Bar/line chart: comparative performance of LLMs and VLMs on rotation tasks across difficulty levels.
Activation heatmap or attention overlay: neurons/heads that respond to rotation-related tokens or prompts.
Illustrated example: sample text prompt describing a scene + annotated rotation transformation and expected model output.
paper_title: How Do LLMs and VLMs Understand Viewpoint Rotation Without Vision? An Interpretability Study
paper_authors: Zhen Yang, Ping Jian, Zhongbin Guo, Zuming Zhang, Chengzhi Li
